key_facts: In or around mid-2024, Plaintiff applied for a position in UPS's delivery and logistics operations in California. As part of its standard pre-employment screening, UPS initiated a background check through First Advantage (fadv.com). On July 22, 2024 at 9:57 AM, Plaintiff received a 'Pre Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS' from First Advantage (DoNotReply@fadv.com) directing him to review the report for 'UNITED PARCEL SERVICE' via a secure portal link. Reminder notices followed on July 23, 2024 (10:00 AM) and July 27, 2024 (10:00 AM). On July 31, 2024 at 9:57 AM — nine days after the original pre-adverse notice — Plaintiff received a 'Final Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS,' confirming UPS had taken final adverse action, definitively denying him employment. UPS provided no written communication identifying any basis for the denial other than the background screening report; no other disqualifying information existed in Plaintiff's application. Plaintiff is a registrant on California's Megan's Law sex offender registry, and alleges on information and belief that the First Advantage report disclosed that status to UPS (together with a statutory disclaimer warning that the information could not lawfully be used for employment purposes) and that UPS used it as the basis for the denial, in violation of Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E).
procedural_status: Pre-filing demand letter transmitted July 12, 2026 to Norman M. Brothers Jr., Esq. (norman.brothers@ups.com), United Parcel Service, Inc. counsel, 55 Glenlake Parkway NE, Atlanta, GA 30328; $85,000 demand; complaint enclosed as Exhibit A; litigation hold notice issued; Pilot settlement precedent (STK-CV-UWT-2026-0007649) cited; response deadline July 26, 2026, 5:00 PM PT. Complaint for Damages filed July 15, 2026, San Joaquin Superior Court — UPS was filed first and received lower case number. Assigned STK-CV-UWT-2026-0009113, Dept. 11B, Hon. Robert T. Waters (same department as Matter 12); CMC January 13, 2027, 8:30 AM; service deadline September 13, 2026 (60 days, CRC 3.110). Case assignment notice issued July 15, 2026 by Deputy Clerk Mia Stipe. SUM-100 Summons issued July 15, 2026 (not yet served). FW-003 Order on Court Fee Waiver GRANTED July 15, 2026. On July 20, 2026, Plaintiff filed a SER-001 Request for Sheriff to Serve Court Papers, directing the Sacramento County Sheriff to serve the Summons, Complaint, and Notice of Case Assignment on UPS's registered agent — CSC - Lawyers Incorporating Service, 2710 Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 150N, Sacramento, CA 95833 (business hours, 9am–5pm) — with a requested service deadline of July 31, 2026. Per the Sacramento County Sheriff's Civil File Status printed July 25, 2026 (Case Manager M. Xiang), the Summons & Complaint was SERVED July 22, 2026 at 12:51 PM (1 attempt) on United Parcel Service, Inc., accepted by Josh Swindell, Authorized Agent — well ahead of the requested July 31, 2026 deadline. The sheriff's civil file itself is marked Closed as of 07/23/2026, which reflects only the completion of the sheriff's service assignment, not any change in the status of the underlying civil action, which remains active before Dept. 11B. LIMITATIONS PERIOD PRESERVED: the July 31, 2024 adverse action created a two-year cutoff of July 31, 2026; filing on July 15, 2026 preserved all time-sensitive claims 16 days before that cutoff, and service has now been completed with time to spare. As with Matter 25 (FedEx), Plaintiff does not possess a copy of the underlying First Advantage background report — the secure portal link expired — so the pleading relies on information-and-belief allegations regarding the report's contents and UPS's use of the registry information. COMPUTED DEADLINES FROM THE JULY 22, 2026 SERVICE DATE: responsive pleading (answer or demurrer) due August 21, 2026 — 30 days from service under CCP §412.20(a)(3); the 30-day count lands on a Friday, so no CCP §12a weekend/holiday adjustment applies. If UPS elects to demur rather than answer, CCP §430.41(a)(2) requires the parties to meet and confer in person or by telephone at least 5 days before that date; the raw 5-day count lands on Sunday, August 16, 2026, so as a practical matter meet-and-confer should be completed by Friday, August 14, 2026. If UPS cannot complete that meet-and-confer in time, its counsel must instead file and serve a declaration by August 21, 2026 explaining the good-faith attempt, which triggers an automatic 30-day extension. As of this writing, no answer, demurrer, or meet-and-confer outreach has been received from UPS. PROOF OF SERVICE MAILED TO THE COURT: on July 28, 2026, Plaintiff mailed the Sheriff's Civil Bureau's signed POS-010 Proof of Service of Summons (Levying Officer File No. 2026026041) to San Joaquin Superior Court, 180 E Weber Ave, Stockton, CA 95202, for filing; the form is executed July 23, 2026 by Sheriff's Authorized Agent Jim Cooper, attesting under penalty of perjury that Deputy F. Conley personally served the Complaint, Notice of Case Assignment and Notice of Hearing, and Summons on July 22, 2026 at 12:51 PM on Josh Swindell, Authorized Agent for United Parcel Service, Inc., C/O CSC - Lawyers Incorporating Service, 2710 Gateway Oaks Dr #150N, Sacramento, CA 95833 (fee $50.00, waived). Expected to arrive and be filed by the clerk on or about July 30, 2026, well ahead of the September 13, 2026 CRC 3.110 proof-of-service deadline. NOTED FOR AWARENESS: same-day/same-court/no-related-case-notice point as discussed in Matter 25 (this matter and Matter 25 were filed the same day in adjacent departments of the same courthouse).
damages: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages or $25,000, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, for each unlawful use of registry information. CONSERVATIVE: ~$33,000 (statutory minimum plus modest emotional distress; no wage documentation on file, since Plaintiff never began working for UPS). MODERATE: ~$85,000 (statutory penalty, ICRAA punitive damages up to $5,000 for willful noncompliance, emotional distress, and partial fee-shifting). AGGRESSIVE: ~$200,000 (aggregation across all six causes of action plus Civil Code § 3294 punitive damages, if discovery yields the actual First Advantage report and confirms willful registry-based denial). As with Matter 25, there are no lost W-2 wages to claim — the primary economic recovery theory is the statutory penalty and lost opportunity/career-advancement damages.
risk: Favorable on the law (PC § 290.46(j)(2)(E) is categorical and exception-free; negligence per se under Evid. Code § 669) but evidentiarily thinner than Matters 22/23 — UPS never issued a written admission naming the registry as the basis for denial, and the complaint pleads UPS's actual use of registry information 'on information and belief' throughout. The First Advantage notices establish the timeline (application → pre-adverse notice → two reminders → 9-day gap → final adverse action). The limitations risk has been eliminated: the July 15, 2026 filing preserved all time-sensitive claims 16 days before the July 31, 2026 two-year cutoff from the July 31, 2024 adverse action. Discovery (subpoena to First Advantage for the underlying report, or UPS's hiring file) would be needed to convert the information-and-belief pleading to a proven claim.
